candidate_relations.reason: The imaging shows diffuse bullous emphysema without the nodules and irregular cyst pattern of pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The transient unconsciousness after drug use does not establish hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and does not explain the lung disease.
There is no trauma or neuroimaging evidence of traumatic brain injury.
Pneumothorax is an acute complication of the severe bullous emphysema rather than the etiologic lung diagnosis.
This label attributes the disease to tobacco and emphasizes a complication, while the reference specifies heroin-induced bullous emphysema.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: smoking rather than heroin etiology plus pneumothorax

candidate_relations.reason: COPD is compatible with emphysematous airflow disease but omits the bullous morphology and heroin etiology.
HIV testing was nonreactive and no HIV-associated pulmonary disorder is supported.
The alpha-1 antitrypsin level was normal.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is broader than and omits the heroin-induced bullous emphysema subtype.
Smoking-related emphysema has a conflicting stated cause and does not preserve the heroin-induced bullous subtype.
Substance-induced lung injury captures the causal family but omits emphysema and bullous morphology.
Cystic lung disease describes the structural family but omits heroin-associated bullous emphysema.
Methamphetamine-induced pneumothorax gives a different drug attribution and describes only the complication.
Substance use disorder is an etiologic context but not the pulmonary disease.
Substance-induced respiratory depression could explain the initial unconsciousness but not the chronic bullous emphysema.
Normal alpha-1 antitrypsin testing argues against deficiency-related COPD.
Spontaneous pneumothorax is a complication of the underlying bullous emphysema.
Substance-induced pneumothorax describes the acute complication but omits the heroin-induced bullous emphysema.
Bullous lung disease captures the structural phenotype but omits emphysema and the heroin cause.
The imaging demonstrates emphysema and bullae rather than a smoking-related interstitial lung disease.
